connect.lead1: Connect your wallet to create a passport.
connect.wcDesc: Tangem, MetaMask mobile, Rainbow — scan QR or approve in the app

noCreator.title: No profile found for this wallet.

list.empty: No passports minted from this wallet yet.

mints.unlimited: Monthly mint limit: unlimited (P/M tier or equivalent).
mints.remaining: Remaining mints this calendar month: {rem} (tier limit {limit}).

tools.lead: Choose a task on this page. Attesting an existing passport (P / M) stays above; minting opens in the section below.

v03Ops.leadProfile: Enter an ODP passport ID and tap Show record to load who issued it, the current owner, revocation, delegation to a link-updater wallet, and fingerprints. If this wallet may act on that passport, use the sections below (transfer ownership, trusted helper for links, revoke, etc.). To mint new passports or see only what you issued from this wallet, use the Passport page — «Your passports» lists passports you created here.
v03Ops.creator: Creator (issuer wallet)
v03Ops.revokedYes: Yes — do not treat as valid.
v03Ops.delegation: Trusted helper who can update links (issuer side)
v03Ops.publishAgentHint: One wallet may update the main JSON link and main image link for all passports you created. Set or remove it from the issuer wallet; it is not per passport.
v03Ops.agentUrlLead: Load the passport above first. As the active helper you may change only the main JSON link and main image link (extra images in the record stay as they are). Fingerprints of the passport data cannot be changed here.
v03Ops.agentUrlSubmit: Save new links to the registry
v03Ops.agentUrlUrlTooLong: Each link must be at most 512 characters.
v03Ops.revokeReason: Reason (a short code derived from your text is stored publicly)
v03Ops.instLeadPm: Only institutional profiles (types P and M) can raise or clear this on-chain flag. Enter the target passport ID in the field above (Show record is optional). The note below is hashed — full text is not stored on-chain.
v03Ops.cfNeedPassportIdInField: Enter a passport ID (ODP-…) in the field above.
v03Ops.cfReason: Short note (stored as a code, not full text)
v03Ops.pAffLead: Parent must be a P-type profile. To propose or confirm a link, use Profile.
v03Ops.pAffProfileLink: Open Profile to propose or confirm →
v03Ops.pAffLeadOnProfile: Here you only unlink a child P profile. To propose or confirm a link, use “Institution structure” above on this page.
v03Ops.notV03: This registry uses older rules — these actions are not available.

manage.loadError: Could not load the passport record.
manage.summaryLead: These tools update only mutable passport fields. Core passport fingerprints stay unchanged.
manage.stateLead: Only changed fields are sent. Each changed block opens its own wallet confirmation because the contract stores these updates separately on-chain.
manage.stateProgress: Confirm update {cur} of {total} in your wallet…
manage.statePartial: Saved {done} of {total} current-state update(s) before an error. The latest on-chain values were reloaded.
manage.linksLead: Main passport and image URLs are edited in the existing hosting URL dialog.
manage.transferLead: This changes the current owner wallet. The creator and passport ID stay the same.
manage.transferSameOwner: That wallet already owns this passport.
manage.auxLead: Optional second commitment such as a COA PDF or conservation file. Leave both fields empty to clear it.
manage.auxNoChanges: No auxiliary commitment changes to save.
manage.auxConfirmWallet: Confirm the commitment update in your wallet…
manage.damageHistoryHint: Optional pointer to a condition, conservation, or damage-history file. Leave both fields empty to clear it.
manage.hashInvalid: Fingerprint must be a 32-byte hex value (0x followed by 64 hex characters).
manage.damagePairRequired: Add a damage history fingerprint when a damage history URL is set.
manage.auxPairRequired: Add a commitment fingerprint when a commitment URL is set.
manage.offlineLead: Build a compact odpOffline v0.1 public payload for QR/NFC use. The raw payload bytes are what the NDPP slot anchors on-chain; any NDEF carrier is only transport and stays separate from the canonical .odpass bundle. Hash match via URL/file ≠ proof from the chip; for the tag use Android companion after EV2.
manage.offlineIncludeState: Include a dated current-state snapshot in the payload (advisory only; on-chain state still wins when online).
manage.offlineNdppModeHint: Use a URL-first NDEF layout for phone taps while keeping the anchored payload in the secondary odp:off record.
manage.ndppUrlHint: Optional HTTPS URL for the same raw public payload bytes. Do not put the Verify page URL here.
manage.offlineSizeTarget: Fits, but above the recommended target
manage.offlineSizeSoft: Fits only near the hard limit
manage.offlineSizeHard: Too large for the target NFC profile
manage.offlineTitleTruncated: Title was truncated to fit the compact payload budget ({n} UTF-8 bytes kept).
manage.offlineAnchoredDifferent: No — generated payload differs from the current on-chain NDPP anchor
manage.offlineExportPreviewNdpp: Verify link first; anchored odp:off payload second
manage.offlineTooLarge: This payload is too large for the current NFC target. Shorten the title or omit the state snapshot.
manage.offlineRecommendSmaller: This payload fits, but it is above the recommended target budget for NTAG 424 DNA.
manage.androidLead: Use these helpers to open the Android companion in the right flow. The guided verifier path is for ordinary scans; EV2, mirror-profile, and writing tools stay in the operator route.
manage.androidTagWriterLead: TagWriter prepares the carrier / tap entry. In NDPP-compatible mode, export a URL-first NDEF: Verify link first, anchored offline payload second.
manage.androidTrustLinkLead: Tag TrustLink can authenticate the chip and read TagTamper state. For the current NTAG 424 deployment, the strongest honest ODP check is the documented mirror-profile comparison against on-chain nfcPublicKey, not a claimed native challenge-response.
manage.androidCopiedHandoff: Android handoff copied or shared. Open it in the guided companion flow.
manage.androidClipboardUnavailable: Clipboard is not available in this browser.
manage.ndppNoChanges: No NDPP / offline-anchor changes to save.
manage.ndppConfirmWallet: Confirm the NDPP / offline-anchor update in your wallet…
manage.notAllowed: This wallet cannot edit the mutable fields shown here for this passport.
manage.revokedLocked: This passport is revoked on-chain. Mutable updates are locked.
manage.transferConfirmWallet: Confirm the ownership transfer in your wallet…
manage.revokeLead: Revocation is irreversible. Verifiers should no longer treat the passport as a valid authenticity anchor after this action confirms on-chain.
manage.revokeNeedAck: Confirm the irreversible revocation checkbox first.
manage.revokeConfirmWallet: Confirm the irreversible revocation in your wallet…

pmProof.calloutBody: Someone asked you to confirm something about a passport that already exists in the public registry. You attach your institution’s confirmation to that passport number only — you are not creating a new passport here.
pmProof.body: When you have the passport number (ODP-…), you can record your expert or museum confirmation in the registry. Optional: fingerprint of a PDF (or other file) and a public link. You pay a small network fee; your profile ID is stored as who confirmed.
pmProof.mintFootnote: To create new passports, open “Mint or update passports” below. P and M types are not limited like C/B for monthly counts.
pmProof.humanIdHint: The passport must already exist in the registry. If the number is wrong or missing, your wallet will show an error.
pmProof.noteFileHelp: Upload a certificate, report, or scan — we build a fingerprint in your browser; only the fingerprint is saved publicly.
pmProof.noteFileDrop2: Processed on your device — file is not uploaded to this site
pmProof.noteUrlHint: Use together with a file above: the registry stores link and fingerprint together.
pmProof.listEmpty: No confirmations recorded for your profile yet.
pmProof.needHumanId: Enter a valid passport number (starts with ODP-).
pmProof.urlNeedsHash: To add a link, upload a file first so a fingerprint exists (the registry requires both together).
pmProof.secCfLead: Separate from a positive proof attestation: record that your institution (P / M) has an authenticity concern about a passport. Enter the target Passport ID below. Optionally attach a file and/or a public link — only a single derived hash is stored on-chain (fingerprints and URL are mixed into that hash).
pmProof.cfPassportIdHint: The passport this concern refers to (can differ from the confirmation block above).
pmProof.cfFileHelp: Optional — certificate, report, or scan. We fingerprint the file in your browser; only the SHA-256 is mixed into the on-chain hash.
pmProof.cfUrlHintCf: Optional public https URL; if present, it is mixed into the on-chain hash together with the file fingerprint (or with an empty file).
pmProof.cfStatusInactive: No active concern flag for this passport in the registry.
pmProof.cfClearOnlyProver: Only the same profile that raised the flag can clear it.
pmProof.cfRevertNoMethod: This registry contract does not support this action (different deployment version).

form.draftRestored: Your unpublished draft was restored in this browser.
form.physicalDesc: Artwork, photography, documents, collectibles — any physical object with a seal
form.mixedDesc: Objects with both physical and digital components registered together
form.requiredSectionLead: Required for mint. Co-authors sit under the title; description and tags have their own block below; other optional fields live in the matching section (physical, digital, preview). Verification method and edition model are set automatically from NFC, C2PA, and edition numbers.
form.groupObjectTypeLead: Choose what you are registering: a physical object, a digital file, or both together. This controls which blocks appear below.
form.groupIdentityLead: How the work is named and classified in the passport.
form.groupTaxonomyLead: Content class, lifecycle status, and AI status go on-chain. How the object is verified (NFC, C2PA, …) is derived from your steps below — not chosen separately.
form.groupHostingLead: Where verifiers can download your .odpass file after mint. You can skip a public link only if the checkbox below is available and you accept offline-only verification.
form.groupDigitalFileLead: The original file is fingerprinted on your device (not uploaded). Register before sharing the raw file publicly.
form.groupDigitalKindLead: Pick the closest type — image, video, 3D, audio, or document.
form.groupSealLead: How this physical object is bound to the passport. Pick one method (or both). NFC with TagTamper needs the Android steps in the block below.
form.groupPeopleOptionalLead: Optional credits beyond the main name on the passport.
form.groupDiscoveryOptionalLead: Optional text for humans and filters. Does not replace on-chain facts.
form.groupPhysicalOptionalLead: Materials, location, condition. Edition number + total → «limited» in the passport; otherwise «unique».
form.groupDigitalOptionalLead: File format label and content-credentials fingerprint, if you use them.
form.groupPreviewOptionalLead: One thumbnail or up to three preview images, plus extra metadata — for Verify and wallets. Not the same as the «Original» file in the digital block.
form.groupExtraV03Lead: Second and third preview images, custom fields, dimensions and weight — only if you need them (passport v0.3+).
form.hintTitle: Public title of the work or object.
form.hintYourName: Creator name as it should appear on the passport (can match your wallet profile).
form.hintCategory: Broad type: artwork, photo, document, collectible, etc.
form.hintYear: Year the work was made (not necessarily the mint date).
form.hintContentClass: Static = one file/snapshot; time-based = video/audio; spatial = 3D; textual = mainly text; composite = mixed; executable = runs as software.
form.hintStatus: Concept = idea stage; prototype = test piece; produced object = finished work; archived = no longer active.
form.hintAiStatus: Whether AI tools were used: none, assisted (human-led), or generated (mainly AI).
form.hintVerificationMethod: How trust is established: self-asserted, institutional, NFC chip, C2PA credentials, or hybrid.
form.hintEditionModel: Unique = one copy; limited = numbered edition; open = unnumbered series; dynamic = changing editions.
form.hintSubtype: What kind of digital file you are registering.
form.hintDescription: Free text for collectors and verifiers.
form.hintDomain: Theme or field, e.g. contemporary_art — helps browsing.
form.hintNfcInstalled: When the NFC chip was placed on the object (today is fine).
form.phLocation: e.g. artist archive, gallery storage, on loan
form.phRightsNote: e.g. personal collection, exhibition rights by request
form.phConditionNote: e.g. excellent, minor edge wear, restored 2025
form.extraMetaHint: Add rows with a name and a value (inventory number, show, internal reference, …). Empty names are ignored. Whatever you fill in is part of the public passport fingerprint.
form.additionalAccordionLead: Everything here is optional. Open only if you need co-authors, a preview image, materials, tags, custom metadata rows, or extra photos.
form.skipPublicUrl: No public file link — create the passport without a web address for the file. The public Verify page then cannot download your passport from the internet; checks need your local .odpass file. You can add a link later under “Update hosting links.”
form.useFolder: Use a folder on my site — after mint, the app registers a path like …/YourPassportID.odpass automatically (one extra confirm in the wallet)
form.folderHint: No filename — just the folder. After you create the passport, upload your .odpass file named ODP-YYYY-MM-NNNNNNNNN.odpass (your real passport number from the success screen, same spelling). The registry will store your-folder/ODP-….odpass.
form.fullUrlHint: Exact public HTTPS URL of the file after you upload it. Use this if you already know the full path (without using the folder option above).
form.hostingInfoTitleFull: How third-party passport file hosting works
form.digitalWarn: ⚠ Register BEFORE sharing the original. Publish only compressed or watermarked versions after.
form.fdropFileLine1: Drop original file or click to select
form.fdropFileLine2: Fingerprint computed on your device — never uploaded
form.fdropImgLine1: Drop image or click to select
form.c2paHint: Only if you use content-credentials software and it gave you a fingerprint for this file.
form.extraImagesHint: Optional extra pictures. Add the main preview above first; each one gets its own fingerprint in the registry.
form.v03MetaHint: All optional. Anything you enter becomes part of the public passport fingerprint.
form.phListingPrice: e.g. 1200 USD — not a legal offer
form.sealLead: A seal binds this passport to the specific physical object. At least one method required.
form.hintSealNfc: NFC + TagTamper: use the Android app steps in the NFC block below (required before mint).
form.hintSealNum: Numbered seal only: fill seal number and type in the «Numbered seal» section when it appears.
form.hintSealBoth: Both: complete NFC steps and numbered seal fields.
form.nfcLead: Three steps on this page: (A) paste the secret key from the Android app after it prepared the chip → (B) scan the chip in the app and import the result → (C) mint. Do not mint before step B shows green.
form.nfcIssuerPixelHint: On one phone: install the ODP Companion app, open this mint page in Chrome, connect your wallet, then follow blocks A and B below.
form.nfcIssuerStepATitle: Step A — after the app prepared the chip (provision)
form.nfcIssuerStepABody: In the Android app: Issue new passport → Provision the chip → hold the tag. Then either copy only the secret key, or copy the whole JSON and press the button below.
form.nfcIssuerChipKeyHint: 32 characters, letters a–f and digits 0–9 only (no spaces). This is the key the app created on the chip — not your wallet key.
form.nfcIssuerProvisionPasteLabel: Or paste the whole JSON from the app (step 1 result)
form.nfcIssuerProvisionPastePh: Paste what the app shows after «Copy provision JSON»
form.nfcIssuerProvisionImportBtn: Take secret key from this JSON
form.nfcIssuerProvisionImportOk: Secret key applied. Now do step B: scan the chip in the app.
form.nfcIssuerProvisionImportEmpty: Paste the JSON from the Android app first.
form.nfcIssuerProvisionImportBadJson: This does not look like valid JSON.
form.nfcIssuerProvisionImportWrongType: This JSON is not from chip provisioning (step 1). Use the export after «Provision the chip», not after the pre-mint scan.
form.nfcIssuerProvisionImportBadKey: The JSON must contain a secret key of exactly 32 hex characters.
form.nfcIssuerProvisionImportFailed: Could not read the provisioning JSON.
form.nfcIssuerStepBTitle: Step B — verify the chip before mint (scan)
form.nfcIssuerStepBBody: In the app: go to «Scan before mint», hold the tag, then tap «Open mint page in browser» or copy the scan JSON and paste it below.
form.nfcIssuerScanPasteLabel: Paste scan result from the app (step B)
form.nfcIssuerScanPastePh: Paste after «Copy chip setup JSON» or return from «Open mint page»
form.nfcIssuerScanPasteHint: Not the same JSON as step A. Step B confirms the seal is intact and fills the chip ID automatically.
form.nfcIssuerStepCBody: When step B shows confirmed, finish the rest of the form and press Mint. The chip ID and blockchain key fields appear below automatically.
form.nfcIssuerPending: Step B not done yet: scan the chip in the Android app first.
form.nfcIssuerConfirmed: Step B OK ({at}). You can mint when the rest of the form is ready.
form.nfcIssuerNeedKey: Complete step A first: paste the chip secret key from the Android app.
form.nfcAutoFilledLead: Filled automatically after step B (you do not type these):
form.labelNfcModelHint: Leave «TagTamper» selected unless your deployment docs say otherwise.
form.nfcIssuerCompanionMissing: Android companion helpers are not loaded on this page.
form.nfcIssuerCopiedHandoff: Companion handoff copied. Open the app on your phone or paste into companion import.
form.nfcIssuerImportOk: Scan result applied. Chip ID and key are ready for mint.
form.nfcIssuerImportEmpty: Paste the scan JSON from the Android app (step B).
form.nfcIssuerImportWrongType: This JSON is from step A (provisioning), not step B. Use «Take secret key from this JSON» in block A, or paste the scan export from «Scan before mint».
form.nfcIssuerImportBadKey: Export must include a 16-byte EV2 key (32 hex chars).
form.nfcIssuerImportEv2Failed: EV2 authentication did not pass on the device scan.
form.nfcIssuerImportTamperOpen: TagTamper seal is not INTACT. Fix the physical seal before mint.
form.validateNfcScanRequired: Complete step B: scan the chip in the Android app before minting.
form.validateNfcKeyLen: Chip secret key must be 32 hex characters (16 bytes).
form.validateNfcUid: Chip sticker ID (UID) must be 14 hex characters (7 bytes).
form.feeLine: This registry (version {gen}): you only pay the Polygon network fee (POL) — no extra service fee from us. Often about US$0.01 (varies).
form.preModalTitle: Your passport file — confirm before minting
form.preWithUrlP1: The public registry stores only a fingerprint of your passport — not the full file. You must keep the correct passport.json and publish it at the link you register. If the file is missing or was edited, checks will fail.
form.preWithUrlP2: After creating the passport you get a .odpass package. Upload that whole file unchanged to your HTTPS folder so the link points to it — e.g. …/YourPassportID.odpass. Verify opens passport.json from inside the ZIP in your browser. You can change the link later (small network fee only) under Update hosting links.
form.preSkipUrlP1: You are creating the passport without a public link to the file. The Verify page will not be able to download your passport from the web until you add a link later.
form.preSkipUrlP2: Only someone who has your .odpass file can check details and authenticity against the registry. Keep the file safe and share it on purpose.
form.preAckWithUrl: I understand: I keep the .odpass file and put it at the registered link if I want strangers to verify over the web. Without the file at that address, others cannot verify online.
form.preAckSkipUrl: I understand: without a public file link, Verify cannot load my passport from the web; only people with my .odpass file can check it against the registry.
form.preAckErr: Check the box to confirm you understand, then continue.
form.hostingModalP1: If you use folder hosting in the form, the app registers your-folder/YourPassportID.odpass for you after mint. Otherwise, paste the full .odpass file URL yourself.
form.hostingModalP2: Verify opens your link in the browser. The answer must be the raw passport file or a .odpass ZIP — not a normal web page, not a login screen, not GitHub’s pretty file page.
form.hostingModalP3: Use HTTPS. The link should open the file directly (browser download or raw file), not a menu page.
form.hostingModalP4: On GitHub: use the “Raw” link (raw.githubusercontent.com…), not the project page. Wait until Raw shows your file.
form.hostingModalP5: On your site or cloud storage: upload the whole .odpass file unchanged. The link path must match where the file really is.
form.hostingModalP6: Some private servers block other sites from loading files; public static hosting usually works. If Verify says it cannot load the file, ask your host about “CORS” or try another host.
form.hostingModalP7: Any edit to the file changes its fingerprint. Upload exactly the .odpass you downloaded when you created the passport.
form.hostingModalP8: You may host plain passport.json instead of .odpass; Verify accepts both. If you use .odpass, the link should end with .odpass.
form.urlModalLead: Change where your .odpass (or plain passport.json) and the optional image are hosted. Only the creator wallet can submit. The passport fingerprint in the registry stays the same — the file at the new address must still be the same content. You only pay a small Polygon network fee (POL).
form.urlDataUrlLabel: Passport file URL — .odpass or raw JSON (optional — leave empty to clear public URL)
form.urlSubmit: Save to registry — network fee only (POL)
form.shareExportLead: Save the full card as an image — title, passport ID, badge, and QR — for posts, prints, or archives.
form.sharePreviewAlt: Card preview — same image as download
form.sharePngLibMissing: Image export library failed to load. Refresh the page and try again.
form.sharePngFail: Could not build the passport card image.
form.sharePngFallbackDl: This browser cannot share image files; the PNG was downloaded instead.
form.validateFolderUrl: Enter a valid HTTPS folder URL (e.g. https://art.com/passport)
form.validateJsonUrl: Passport file URL (.odpass or raw JSON) is required
form.validateDigitalFile: Original file is required for digital objects
form.validateNfc: NFC chip UID and public key are required
form.validateSeal: Seal number and type are required
form.validateC2pa: The manifest fingerprint must look like a long hex code from your tool (often shown as sha256:… or starting with 0x).
form.validateExtraImagesFirst: Add the main preview image above before extra images.
form.validateNeedImage2Before3: Use additional images in order: add image 2 before image 3, or clear image 3 first.
form.txWaitHelp: After you approve in the wallet, mining can take a minute. Leave this tab open. If the spinner stays long, open the explorer link — when the transaction shows as successful, return here; the page should continue automatically. Avoid refreshing unless the transaction failed or you use “Back to form” below.
form.mintErrorHint: Your form data was kept where possible — use “Back to form”. If the transaction actually succeeded, check the explorer before minting again.
form.odpassDlAlert: Could not save the .odpass file automatically. In MetaMask’s browser, use “Share” when offered and pick Save to Files, or open the site in Safari/Chrome and try Download again.
form.mintConfirmWallet: Please confirm the transaction in your wallet
form.mintRegisteringUrl: Saving file link to the registry…
form.mintUrlFail: Mint succeeded, but updating the public file URL failed. Use URLs next to this passport in the list below and set the .odpass (or raw JSON) URL to:
form.mintReadHumanId: Could not read Passport ID from mint receipt.
form.successUploadWithUrl: Upload your .odpass file unchanged to this exact HTTPS link (same file as you downloaded here so the fingerprint matches the registry). Verify reads passport.json from inside the ZIP in your browser:
form.successNoPublicUrl: No public file link is saved in the registry yet. Share the downloaded .odpass only with people who must check it. You can add a link later under Update hosting links.
form.successStep2: Tap Share next to Download: save the full passport card as PNG or send it from your device.
form.successStep3: Make sure your profile ID {creatorId} is published on your website and social profiles.
form.successIphoneHint: iPhone / MetaMask in-app browser: a plain download may not appear in Files. After downloading .odpass, use the browser or Files app share menu (Save to Files / iCloud), then upload the file to your host unchanged.
form.successDidHint: Optional extra identity file (DID) — you can build it anytime from registry data, including for older passports.
form.odpassModalBody: You can download your .odpass bundle from this page only during this visit. This site does not store it on a server — after you leave, you cannot retrieve this file here again.
form.odpassModal321: Back it up using a 3-2-1 rule: keep at least three copies, on two different types of storage, with one copy off-site (another location or a cloud provider you trust).
form.leaveSuccessConfirm: Leave this screen? Make sure your .odpass file is saved in a safe place. Continue?
form.qrFail: QR library did not load (network / CDN blocked).

urlEdit.urlTooLong: Each URL must be at most 512 characters

errors.connectInProgress: Connection already in progress. Approve or reject the request in your wallet extension, then try again.
errors.walletPending: A wallet request is already open. Use the wallet extension icon in the toolbar to approve or cancel — do not click Connect again until that finishes.

noWallet.line1: No wallet in this browser. On a computer, install
noWallet.mmHint: iPhone / Safari: there is no extension — MetaMask runs as an app with a built-in browser. This link opens the same page there so Connect works.
noWallet.fileProto: Local file URLs — many wallets do not work. Run a simple web server for the web folder or use HTTPS.
noWallet.httpsHint: Use https:// or http://localhost if needed.
noWallet.wcLead: Or connect a phone wallet (e.g. Tangem) via WalletConnect — no browser extension required.
